evidence.description: The timer interval is calculated using 1 divided by investmentPerSecond, which could result in a very small value if investmentPerSecond is large, potentially leading to high-frequency execution.

candidates.explanation: The calculation for 'secondsToOneEuro' does not have a minimum floor other than 1, but if investmentPerSecond is very high, the logic relies entirely on that value. Furthermore, if investmentPerSecond is 0, it defaults to 1, but if it is a very large number, the frequency of timer events could impact performance.
candidates.title: Potential for infinite loop or high-frequency updates

evidence.description: The class accesses Statistics.shared directly multiple times.
The class accesses Statistics.shared directly inside totalInvestedAt.

candidates.explanation: Directly accessing a shared singleton (Statistics.shared) makes the class harder to test in isolation and creates a tight coupling between InvestmentsProjection and the Statistics class.
candidates.title: Hardcoded dependency on a shared singleton

evidence.description: The class maintains a manual array of subscriptions.

candidates.explanation: While the class conforms to Publisher, it manually manages a list of subscriptions. If not managed correctly (e.g., adding but never removing), this could lead to memory leaks or unintended behavior, as the class does not appear to implement the standard Combine lifecycle for managing subscribers.
candidates.title: Manual management of subscriptions
